spec.full_target: For every n∈ℕ and E⊆ℝ^n, if E is nonempty and compact, then for I=[0,1] and the concatenated Euclidean metric on E×I, dim_H(E×I)=dim_H(E)+1.

calculations: Coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz in the concatenated Euclidean metric. For subsets U⊆ℝ^n and J⊆ℝ, diam(U×J)≤√(diam(U)^2+diam(J)^2). Subdivide [0,1] into at most 1/r+1 intervals of length at most r when 0<r≤1.

primitives.meaning: The n-dimensional real inner-product space, including the singleton ℝ^0.
Critical exponent of Hausdorff measures, with empty-set dimension zero.

propositions.statement: For a set A in a Borel extended metric space and d≥0, if d<dim_H(A), then the d-dimensional Hausdorff measure of A is infinite.

source.statement: hausdorffMeasure_of_lt_dimH: if (d:ℝ≥0)<dimH A then μH[d] A=∞.
hypotheses: A set in an extended metric space with the Borel measurable structure required by Mathlib's hausdorffMeasure and dimH declarations; d is an NNReal.

propositions.statement: For a Lipschitz map f between extended metric spaces and any set A in its domain, dim_H(f '' A)≤dim_H(A).

source.statement: LipschitzWith.dimH_image_le: a Lipschitz map does not increase Hausdorff dimension of an image.
hypotheses: X and Y are extended metric spaces; K:NNReal; f:X→Y is LipschitzWith K; s⊆X.

propositions.statement: For a finite-dimensional real normed space V and set A⊆V with nonempty interior, dim_H(A)=finrank(ℝ,V).

source.statement: Real.dimH_of_nonempty_interior: if a set in a finite-dimensional real normed space has nonempty interior, its Hausdorff dimension is the finrank of the space.
hypotheses: V is a finite-dimensional real normed space and interior(A) is nonempty.

propositions.statement: For a countable family of nonnegative measurable functions, the integral of their pointwise sum is the sum of their integrals.

source.statement: lintegral_tsum: lintegral of a countable sum of nonnegative extended-real functions equals the sum of their lintegrals, provided every summand is almost-everywhere measurable.
hypotheses: A measurable space with a measure; a countable index type; each summand is AEMeasurable into ENNReal.

argument.text: Write D=dim_H(E), F=E×[0,1], with distance squared |x−y|²+|t−u|². The compact set E is bounded in ℝ^n; covering a bounded Euclidean box by O(k^n) cubes of diameter O(1/k) shows H^q(E)=0 for every q>n, so D is finite. The threshold characterization then gives H^q(E)=0 whenever q>D. Fix q>D. At every scale δ≤1, choose a cover of E by sets of positive diameters r_j≤δ with arbitrarily small sum Σr_j^q. Zero-diameter members are singletons; replace each by a positive-diameter ball of diameter at most δ, choosing added q-cost summable and arbitrarily small. Cover I for each j by at most 1/r_j+1 intervals of length at most r_j. The corresponding products have diameter at most √2r_j and total (q+1)-cost at most 2(√2)^(q+1)Σr_j^q. Their maximum diameters tend to zero with δ, and cost tends to zero; hence H^(q+1)(F)=0 and dim_H(F)≤D+1.

For the lower bound when D>0, fix 0<s<D. By M001, H^s(E)=∞. Consequently the scale-s contents c_s(E,δ) tend to infinity as δ decreases to zero: these contents are monotone as the scale decreases and their limit defines H^s. For an arbitrary countable cover V_i of F with ρ_i=diam(V_i)≤δ≤1, project to A_i⊆ℝ^n and B_i⊆I. Then diam(A_i),diam(B_i)≤ρ_i. Enlarge each B_i into an open interval J_i of length ≤ρ_i+η_i, with η_i>0 and Ση_iρ_i^s<ε. For every t∈I, the A_i for which t∈J_i cover E: for every x∈E, (x,t) belongs to some V_i, so t∈B_i⊆J_i. Thus c_s(E,δ)≤Σ_i 1_{J_i}(t)ρ_i^s pointwise. These interval indicators are measurable; Tonelli M004 and integration over I yield c_s(E,δ)≤Σ_i |J_i∩I|ρ_i^s≤Σ_iρ_i^(s+1)+ε. Terms with ρ_i=0 contribute zero since s>0. Let ε→0 and take the infimum over all product covers to obtain c_s(E,δ)≤c_(s+1)(F,δ). The left side tends to infinity as δ→0, so H^(s+1)(F)=∞ and M001's converse threshold implication (equivalently the definition of dim_H) gives dim_H(F)≥s+1. As this holds for every 0<s<D, dim_H(F)≥D+1.

If D=0, choose x₀∈E using H001. The coordinate projection π:F→I, π(x,t)=t, is 1-Lipschitz by the displayed Euclidean distance and is onto because (x₀,t)∈F for each t. Its image has dimension 1: I has nonempty interior in ℝ, and M003 gives dim_H(I)=finrank(ℝ,ℝ)=1. Applying M002 to π and F gives 1=dim_H(I)≤dim_H(F)=D+1. Combining with the upper bound proves equality. This works unchanged when n=0, since E is then a nonempty subset of a singleton and π remains onto.

hypothesis_checks: Apply to X=ℝ^n with its Euclidean Borel metric, A=E and real s>0 with s<D; thus s<dim_H(E) and the Hausdorff measure is infinite.
The coordinate map π has Lipschitz constant 1 for the concatenated Euclidean distance; the set is F.
Apply with V=ℝ and A=[0,1], whose interior contains (0,1); finrank(ℝ,ℝ)=1.
Use counting measure on I and the nonnegative measurable summands ρ_i^s·1_{J_i∩I}; each is measurable because J_i is open.
